page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine tailored for input-output intensive and data-heavy enterprise environments. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C x86_64 processor operating at 2.7 GHz, the instance delivers 22 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 11 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory architecture supplies 176 GB of total capacity, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A central characteristic of this instance is its direct-attached storage subsystem, which bundles 9663 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across three physical drives. Acceleration hardware such as GPUs is not included.

The CPU includes hardware vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Across benchmark evaluations, the instance posted a PassMark CPU score of 28161.46 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 11804.0. Its memory subsystem demonstrates uncached read throughput of 107.35 GB/s alongside cached small-block bandwidth of 1494.87 GB/s. For in-memory lookups, it achieved 24.07 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks, while also sustaining 298.77 tokens per second during small-model text generation inference.

By integrating high-capacity local NVMe drives directly with substantial system memory, the instance delivers high resource density for workloads constrained by disk throughput and access latency. However, because local NVMe disks are ephemeral, data durability must be managed through application-level replication. This hardware profile is engineered for high-throughput relational and non-relational database clusters, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching nodes, and heavy indexing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads. It features 22 dedicated vCPUs on an 11-core Intel Xeon 8481C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, equipped with AVX-512 and Intel AMX extensions. System memory totals 176 GB, offering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware platform integrates 9663 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage across three local drives, delivering high input/output bandwidth without GPU hardware. Benchmarks show consistent mid-tier compute capabilities with a PassMark CPU score of 28161.46 and 24.07 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. The pairing of substantial RAM and extensive local NVMe capacity provides high resource density for disk-bound services, though local storage ephemerality demands replication architectures. It is targeted at distributed transactional databases, analytics nodes, indexing pipelines, and high-performance caching infrastructure.
